We establish a precise relationship between L^p to L^q contraction inequalities in weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk, incorporating typical weight factors and examining both absolute and conformal invariance implications.

This study investigates a novel, data-efficient AI-based COVID-19 diagnosis system. By analyzing 100 low-dose CT scans with an average of only 2 per case, we develop a two-stage time-distributed capsule network. The first stage generates capsule representations, while the second uses them to classify patients as COVID-19 positive or negative. To evaluate performance accurately, we employ the maximum mean discrepancy metric, measuring the distance between real and predicted labels, combined with cross-entropy loss. Consequently, the trained model achieves a remarkable 97% classification accuracy on low-dose CT scans. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of efficiency and low-dose CT scan interpretation capabilities.

As more satellites in low-Earth orbit facilitate Earth observation, internet access, and other applications, concerns have grown regarding space occupancy. Research in this paper examines two key aspects: first, it models how satellites' positions spread out over time due to gravitational influences and other perturbations, including how initial satellite placement affects this effect in plans like Starlink. Various observations are demonstrated to support this model, including the spreading out of Starlink satellites and the identification of stable orbital zones. Second, this paper discusses how these orbital constraints impact the design of satellite constellations, highlighting the importance of horizontal spacing between satellites to minimize disturbances, as shown in calculations for a hypothetical Starlink-like configuration.

To efficiently simulate aerodynamic flow around complex objects, we develop a novel method for automatically generating high-order quadrilateral meshes from Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models. By employing integer linear programming techniques, we optimize key features of the mesh generation process, including the levels of quadrilateral elements and their arrangement. Our technique involves a two-phase method: initially, we identify regions that cannot be meshed using quadrilaterals and convert them into lower-order elements, and then we optimize the remaining quadrilateral mesh based on its desired characteristics. Extensive testing on various objects has demonstrated the effectiveness of our method in producing high-quality meshes.

Pearson's correlation coefficient is frequently employed in neuroscience to measure the strength of relationships between neural activity patterns. Research has recently gained interest in exploring permutation-based methods, particularly Sample Correlation with permutation testing, where results are compared to empirical permutation distributions. Although such studies rely heavily on simulations, we establish exact mathematical formulas for the moments of correlation distributions under various data transformations, including data permutations. These formulas, developed for datasets of any size and dimensions, are fundamental in permutation-based analysis and may also aid in understanding the correlation distribution's underlying structure. We have applied our results to solve key statistical moments of Sample Correlation and explore how its distribution changes as dataset parameters increase.

We detail the reasoning behind employing a scattering matrix approach to understand scattering probabilities in a generalized gravitational framework, incorporating higher-order curvature interactions. Furthermore, an additional hypothesis is introduced to examine high-energy events in the context of the Standard Model, while also noting that this assumption shares conceptual similarities with tree-level gravitational properties.

This paper presents a novel approach to controlling two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, employing a multidimensional feedback control scheme in an unbounded domain. Using a spectral theory-based analysis with the help of the Hadamard inverse theorem and the Banach perturbation theorem, we demonstrate the system's uniform stabilizability in various Sobolev and Besov spaces against increasingly smaller initial disturbances within an $L^\infty$-norm bounded range. Our control strategy involves a finite, localized function over the entire space $\mathbb{R}^2$, and we establish the existence and regularity of the controlling force within the same regularity class as the controlled system variables. Notably, our work also highlights the significant impact of the chosen control strategy on the system's stabilizability issues.

Language learning dictionaries are pivotal tools in acquiring and comprehending 
a new language. As liturgical languages such as Syriac and Arabic are used by 
religions for which numerous educational resources are limited, they require 
a dictionary to facilitate learning. To address this need, we've created LitMind, 
an open-source online dictionary that can be accessed at https://litmind.net, or 
downloaded as a desktop application. LitMind contains a comprehensive collection 
of 88,139 Syriac and 188,706 Arabic words paired with their corresponding 
English definitions, along with images for 16,770 and 75,070 words respectively.

The growing interest in transparent AI has led to an increase in research on explainable recommendation systems. Among these, post-hoc methods that uncover implicit recommendation model reasoning have gained significant attention. However, existing post-hoc explanations in recommendation systems fall short of meeting rigorous verification criteria for constituting genuine explanations. This study aims to bridge this gap by adapting the LIME method for use in recommendation systems and exploring its utility as a post-hoc explanation method. Through theoretical analysis, characteristics of the modified LIME method are identified, and its performance compared to existing post-hoc recommendation explanations is evaluated. Moreover, a novel verification framework based on theoretical constants is proposed, and its effectiveness assessed. Finally, experiments assessing the adherence of LIME-generated explanations to item feature contexts are conducted and analyzed.

Quantum devices based on thin semiconductor layers close to the surface are very sensitive to surface properties because of surface fermi level pinning. In near-surface InAs quantum wells, even small changes in metal contacts can lead to highly non-ohmic behavior due to pinning, and researchers investigated how an aluminum oxide passivation layer can mitigate this issue. The experiment showed that ALD passivation reduces pinning effects and creates a more uniform current distribution within the quantum structure as evidenced by photoluminescence data. Furthermore, ALD passivation increases the time between electron recombination events by 30% and increases the power handling capacity of light-emitting devices by 40% when compared to plasma etched devices. The ALD passivation technique has the potential to improve the performance of light emitters, lasers, and photodetectors in near surface quantum structures.

We investigate the robustness of classification models in environments where the data collector can be compromised by an adversary. Our research reveals the critical role of local query access in achieving robust learning under adversarial conditions. Specifically, we demonstrate that local knowledge can enable the robust one-bit classification of concepts from a broad class of functions defined by limited influence points. Conversely, we show that attempting to attain robustness without local query access results in failure when dealing with data influenced by small subsets of points. Notably, we establish this failure in scenarios where the adversary's capabilities are minimal. Our findings are significant as they show that the absence of local query access renders the robust classification of intricate patterns, such as lines in high-dimensional space, unattainable even when dealing with single-bit labels.

Our previous research significantly sped up Sinkhorn iteration by linearizing its complexity through the application of an initial value from Correntropy $L_1$ norm. This approach was successful due to its convergence properties. However, our model was limited and couldn't handle more complex cases. In this paper, we propose a more versatile framework, capable of processing general positive matrices while linearizing the complexity. We specifically focus on a subset of matrices - the collinear triangular matrices - because they can be manipulated in linear time. These matrices come from the T-transform, which is highly relevant in optimal transport applications. We developed a new iterative algorithm for computing the T-transform via the T-segmentation process and applied it to accelerate the Sinkhorn iteration. We tested the performance of the new algorithm using a synthetic example, comparing it with existing methods like Sinkhorn and Kernel Two-Sample Tests. The results showed that the new algorithm outperforms these methods, and it has significant implications for real-world applications in image processing and computer vision, where optimal transport is used.

AU Mic, a M8V star, hosts a protoplanter disk and two close-in planets. Observations of AU Mic in the FUV, focusing on H I, CII, and NO, revealed a smaller disk size in the FUV compared to optical and near-infrared wavelengths. The process responsible for these observations is likely dominated by photoemission. Furthermore, the study found that the luminosity of the AU Mic star increased significantly during flares, and the resulting radiation could trigger atmospheric outflows in the AU Mic b and c planets via a process known as photoevaporation.

This study explores the friction caused by radiation reaction in the presence of a material medium, which is relevant in nuclear collisions and heavy ion experiments. By examining the motion of test particles in the medium, we find that the self-force acting on a particle is proportional to the drag force, which is a function of the medium's nematic order tensor. Notably, the direction and magnitude of the drag force are influenced by the local symmetries of the order tensor, leading to varied levels of friction along different axes.

The effectiveness of the k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) algorithm on classification problems is typically influenced by the distribution of classes. This paper focuses on the application of kNN on datasets that are unevenly distributed. Building upon Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence's ability to quantify the distance between probability distributions, a new statistical measure, relative odds ratio (OR), is introduced to assess class separation. A kNN variant, kNN-OR, is then proposed that utilizes OR instead of Euclidean distance to identify the nearest neighbors of unseen data. Three synthesized datasets and 21 unbalanced datasets are used to compare kNN-OR with the traditional kNN algorithm, demonstrating its superior performance in the majority of cases.

We have identified 20 Ultra-Luminous Quasars (ULQs) spanning a 30-year magnitude range and a redshift interval of 2.1 to 4.7, thanks to the inclusion of quasars exceeding a bolometric luminosity of $10^{41}$ erg/s, as determined from the SkyMapper survey. Our comprehensive dataset includes photometric and spectroscopic observations, as well as estimates of their bolometric luminosity, for all 20 ULQs. Notably, 12 of these quasars were previously unknown, while 8 were previously identified as ULQs. By incorporating our findings, we now possess a comprehensive dataset of 107 quasars at $z>2$ with bolometric luminosities greater than $10^{40}$ erg/s. Analysis of this dataset reveals that the luminosity function for these quasars is characterized by a steep decline at higher luminosivities, with the number of quasars decreasing by a factor of approximately 1000 at bolometric luminosities of $10^{46}$ erg/s, compared to a factor of 100 at $10^{43}$ erg/s. Our results indicate that the inclusion of photometric data for all quasars significantly alters the shape of the luminosity function at the highest luminosities, where it becomes significantly steeper than previously reported.

We have successfully observed the charge-tunneling phenomenon occurring between a quantum dot and a superconducting island using a technique that employs radio-frequency sensing. Our approach has allowed us to directly measure and distinguish the transition frequencies associated with both the Pauli and Cooper tunneling processes without relying on any existing theoretical models. By employing this direct measurement method, we have been able to validate a theoretical calculation previously made on the charge-tunneling mechanism based on our island sensing data.

Our research explores the contraction behavior of specific types of shockwaves in systems of equations, particularly in relation to the L1 norm and convex functions, in systems involving multiple laws. The main findings extend previous work by creating more broad criteria that define suitable shockwave behaviors, in systems involving strictly convex functions, in 2D and 3D spaces. The new criteria are more inclusive in that they cover a variety of strict convexity conditions, such as those seen in systems governing gas flow and generalised gas dynamics. The strategy used in this study involves transforming the strict convex conditions into strict diagonal forms and applying a novel method of measuring the behavior of the shockwaves through an integrated measure. The strict convex conditions are translated into a set of linear inequalities that can be evaluated using a specialized measure for the shockwave, in addition to requiring that the system be in a balanced state following a particular shockwave, in 2D spaces. The work in 3D spaces is more complex and involves examining the behavior of the shockwaves through a specialized measure for the shockwave, in addition to requiring that the system be in a balanced state following the shockwave, in 3D spaces. The broader implications of our work are significant, providing new insights into the behavior of shockwaves in complex systems of equations and opening up new avenues of research in this area.

We present a novel, generative model, DiffDreamer, that creates a continuous exploration of virtual 3D environments from a singular perspective image, like watching an endless, spinning 360-degree video. By building on recent advancements in conditional diffusion models, our approach learns to generate a dynamic sequence of views that maintains spatial consistency over time. We successfully test and validate the model on standard datasets of synthetic and real-world images, discovering that it surpasses current state-of-the-art performance on our evaluation benchmarks.

This work introduces a novel data-driven framework for analyzing and managing complex dynamic networks, including processes like transportation, communication systems, and urban planning. To effectively handle these complex systems, we leverage data to create a simplified mathematical model that captures the interconnected dynamics at play and can be optimized or controlled efficiently. To achieve this, we first develop a modular data-driven method to create a simplified model for each individual process, which, when applied to multiple interconnected processes, naturally yields a simplified mathematical model for the entire complex network. To further demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework, we test it on a network model of disease spread, showing that it can successfully identify the transmission patterns between different regions, even when multiple distinct patterns coexist. Additionally, we apply data-driven control techniques to force transmission patterns that minimize infected populations. Our framework demonstrates that this approach can successfully manage complex networked systems using only available data, without requiring any prior knowledge of the system's dynamics or parameters.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber heavily depend on the boundary conditions at the fiber's surface. In this study, we investigate how different levels of slip at the fiber's surface influence the behavior of capillary waves and their subsequent evolution. By using a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, we discovered that increased slip at the fiber's surface significantly decreases the amplitude of capillary waves and their eventual instability. Furthermore, we found that waves with nodes closer to the fiber's surface, as opposed to those with peaks, tend to break under the increased slip conditions. Our results, which are supported by the simulations, are also compared with experimental data, showing a significant agreement.

We investigate the temporal Lipschitz stability for solutions of the Hunter-Saxton equation, focusing on $\alpha$-dissipative solutions with $\alpha$ a constant. We introduce and study the properties of new metrics tailored to this specific equation, particularly within a Lagrangian framework, in order to evaluate the distance between solutions. These metrics exhibit natural characteristics and are suitable for analyzing the given equation type, and they also show applicability to other equations of this nature.

Evaluating scoliosis with ultrasound imaging is typically conducted manually by trained personnel. For research purposes, a scanning technique using a robotic arm has been proposed to assess the reliability of ultrasound image analysis in scoliosis patients. This approach was tested by comparing the reliability of robotic and manual scoliosis curve measurement through ultrasound. Two patients underwent 10 ultrasound scans by the robot, and the same scans were analyzed by a physician both manually and by ultrasound with the aid of a specialist. In each case, the variability of the measurements obtained and curve angles were assessed using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient. Robotic and manual measurements showed high reliability, whereas specialist measurements with ultrasound showed lower reliability. Specifically, the robotic and manual measurements yielded an ICC of 0.98, whereas specialist measurements yielded an ICC of 0.82 for scoliosis curve angle measurements. This research confirmed that scoliosis curve angle measurement using the robotic and manual techniques was highly reliable. Furthermore, integrating a specialized system for ultrasound imaging in scoliosis improved the reliability of the measurements compared to the traditional manual method.

This paper introduces an innovative method for duration modelling in statistical parametric speech synthesis by training a deep neural network to generate dynamic phonetic context-based speech duration values for each phone in a phone and tone unit. The main advantage of this approach is that it doesn't require any form of data compression or encoding. The model is applied to real data to calculate Mandarin Chinese speech durations, which are then combined with a small pre-learned phone and tone category table using a deep neural phone classifier. The model is tested on a development dataset and compared with a traditional Gaussian mixture model-based approach and other duration-based syntheses. The results show that the pre-learned table approach is comparable to or sometimes surpasses the traditional method in terms of synthesis duration accuracy and naturalness.

This study introduces a novel framework for detecting hate speech on the social media platform Twitter. The technique combines two different types of automatic feature selection techniques, bag of words and n-grams, to identify the most significant words within online content. The framework relies on a functional XGBoost model trained on the Twitter Hate Speech dataset to classify tweets about hate. The proposed framework's performance was evaluated and compared against a machine learning-based classifier, showcasing its effectiveness. The results reveal that this approach offers easy scalability and can be integrated into automated moderation tools for identifying and preventing hate speech on Twitter.

Multi-input multi-output (MIMO) networks, a prominent deep learning architecture, utilize multiple parallel sub-networks to process input data, as seen in diverse applications. A fundamental issue with MIMO networks is the costly memory requirements for storing the parameters of each sub-network. This paper explores a novel approach to reduce the memory burden of MIMO networks, specifically focusing on promoting shared feature development across sub-networks during training, as well as developing an analysis framework to quantify the degree of feature sharing within MIMO architectures and its practical utility.

This study offers a comprehensive overview of datasets comprising historical documents depicted as images. These documents encompass a diverse range of formats such as handwritten notes from centuries past, the scripts of bygone eras, and the print styles of earlier times. Given the significance of historical documents in our understanding of our heritage, extensive effort has been devoted to developing such datasets for research purposes. Unfortunately, these datasets are often scattered across various publications and conferences, necessitating a systematic compilation to facilitate the evaluation of current methods and identify areas for improvement in the analysis of historical documents. This survey seeks to consolidate the existing datasets on historical documents to provide a more accessible and organized reference for the analysis of historical documents, aiming to facilitate the exploration of this intriguing research area.

We investigated the feasibility of using the flatness property to develop a high-performance control approach for an industrial robot joint with the aid of secondary sensors. Flatness facilitates the creation of reference trajectories that can be realized in an ideal scenario by a feedforward control mechanism, while incorporating this concept with a simple feedback control loop enables the compensation for uncertainties and disturbances present in the system. We focused on the design of the feedforward and feedback control loops as well as on the design of sensors to ensure accurate and reliable velocity and position measurements. Ultimately, the proposed controller was evaluated through experiments on an industrial robot joint and demonstrated its adaptability to different configurations of the flexible-joint motor system.

The objective of Multiple State Analysis is to provide a comprehensive, multidimensional understanding of multiple time-to-event data by mapping an individual's state transitions. In contrast to traditional survival analysis, MSA seeks to capture the complex health patterns that develop over an individual's lifetime. Our study focuses on the effects of myocardial infarction (MI) using administrative data from a large population, where we model the post-MI state transitions using both covariate-based and unobserved-state approaches. Our results reveal that, on average, an MI significantly increases mortality risk within 10 years and that lifestyle factors significantly impact post-MI outcomes, with engaging in sports activities and smoking having significant effects. Notably, our study also found evidence of hidden health states, which may represent chronic conditions or frailty.

This study proposes an innovative multivendor approximation strategy for accurately modeling electrons in complex molecular systems scattered under various potentials. Building upon the established Born-Oppenheimer framework, the method involves approximating continuous wave functions on a carefully discretized grid that can handle the irregular and dispersed nature of these functions. Each potential well is individually addressed using standard one-dimensional techniques, while a central region is modeled separately to ensure a comprehensive and seamless representation of the wave function. The approach is validated through application to the hydrogen molecular ion and a simulated molecular model, demonstrating its efficacy and precision.

In a graph, a subset of vertices forms a resolving set if, for any two vertices, a single set vertex is positioned at different distances from the two vertices. The problem of finding a resolving set of size at most k, called the Metric Dimension problem, has been a subject of research since the 1970s. The problem has been proven to be NP-hard, and while it was found to be not well-behaved under standard parameterization by the size of the solution set, it was shown to be well-behaved when parameterized by the size of a feedback vertex set and other structural parameters, such as the number of vertices with high degree and the number of vertices involved in certain graph patterns. The proof of these results relies on the use of the problem's relationship to other known problems, as well as the use of the problem's behavior under the taking of specific graph operations.

Domain theory's power domains serve as fundamental tools for modeling the relationship between program semantics and model constructions that arise from model theory's boolean and algebraic structures.  We generalize power domain models to a broader class of spaces known as T_0 directed complete spaces, rather than being limited to power domains of domains or algebraic T_0 spaces.  This approach reveals that key power domain models - including the lower, upper, and cubic models - intrinsically possess a directed space structure, and we find that they are categorially equivalent when constructed from directed complete spaces.  Furthermore, we demonstrate that the identity between the power domains of directed spaces and partial maps of directed complete spaces remains valid, and we show that the cubic model can be universally applied across directed complete spaces.

Past Earth climates, when temperatures soared, were known as hothouses and occurred on multiple occasions.
Investigations of these periods, often conducted using simplified computer models, revealed that liquid water could exist on the surface and that it would also be present on the ground.
Our own simulations confirm this outcome, showing however, that there could be significant changes in the weather and that heavy rain might occur at certain times.
A cold spell in the middle of this hothouse period, lasting around 600 years, could result in global ice and severe weather, including storms and lightning.
As the climate warmed again, this could lead to an end to the hothouse period and an transition to another state.
Our research suggests that past hothouse periods might not have been steady and that there could have been times of severe weather, like floods that occurred in the past.
This is a potential danger for Earth-like planets that experience temperature fluctuations during hot periods in other stars' climates.

We've established an inverse transform between Penrose transform based higher-spin fields and Yang-Mills fields, which we used to prove the equivalence of the T[PSYM] model and the self-dual sector of the T$^{\beta\beta}$YM model in flat space. This led to a new method for constructing the $\beta$-deformed T$^{\beta\beta}$YM model and flat space Penrose transform based higher-spin string theory.

The accuracy of deep learning-based medical image classification is severely compromised by label noise in the training dataset, which significantly reduces the reliability of the model. Current approaches to mitigating this issue primarily focus on optimizing the network parameters or employing data augmentation techniques. However, these solutions often overlook the label noise problem at the data level. To address this, we propose a novel method called BS-LRM, designed to minimize the impact of label noise during medical image classification. The Bayesian Statistics-guided Label Refurbishment Mechanism (BS-LRM) involves three key stages: (1) developing a Bayesian-based noise detector to identify noisy samples, (2) generating pseudo-labels for noisy images, and (3) refining the dataset labels through noise correction. The method leverages the probabilistic framework to determine the noise probability distribution and adjust network parameters accordingly. Furthermore, it integrates data augmentation and regularization techniques to optimize the rebagged dataset and refine the network, thereby mitigating the bias introduced by noisy labels. Experimental results across multiple public medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming the current state-of-the-art methods and the baseline models.

Consider a unit cube $Q$ and a subset $E$ within it such that $|Q\setminus E|/|Q|<\epsilon$, where $\epsilon$ is a small positive value less than $1/4$. For any function $f$ in $C(Q)$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, let's suppose an interpolation set $\{x_{k}\}_{k=1}^{N}$ and its corresponding interpolation polynomial $I_{\epsilon}f$. Under the given conditions, $\|I_{\epsilon}f\|_{Q}\leq C(\epsilon)\|f\|_{Q}$ holds true. The constant $C(\epsilon)$ depends solely on $\epsilon$. Moreover, $I_{\epsilon}f$ satisfies the inequality $C(\epsilon)\leq \exp(C_{0}/\sqrt[3]{\epsilon})$. Here, $C_{0}$ represents a positive constant determined by the geometry of the cube $Q$.

A correlated random walk (CRW) is derived from the Grover matrix, the evolution matrix of the Grover walk on a graph G, and an explicit characteristic polynomial for the CRW's transition probability matrix is presented in this study. Furthermore, it is confirmed that Freedman's conjecture holds true.

In a total functions context, functions are guaranteed to find a solution to an equation, but may result in infinite loops for certain inputs. A common initialization process is used to set up the search for these solutions. We are proposing a formal way to incorporate this initialization process into a proof assistant with a specific theory called HOL. Initially, we redefined the implicit search process that the proof assistant uses to solve equations to make it clearer and more explicit. Then, we introduced a new type to represent functions that change over time, similar to how recursive functions work but without considering the input, and used this new type to represent the state during the search process. We also developed a method to introduce new initialization functions for this search process, allowing them to progress over time. Finally, we created a theory to prove equality between functions that change over time and ordinary total functions by considering their equality at different stages of change.

This paper proposes a novel strategy for enhancing structural-based models that predict instantaneously wall-bound flows. The core of this approach lies in refining velocity field estimates by refining the difference field between real and predicted configurations. A key component of this field captures the influence of unresolved scales on the resolved ones. In this work, the distinction between actual and simulated differences is enhanced through data-driven training. The training dataset, consisting of synthetic data, is generated using direct numerical simulation. The synthetic data's relevance to the real data is assessed using the Wilson correlation coefficient and its associated confidence intervals. The effectiveness of the synthetic data in mitigating the discrepancy between the real and synthetic datasets is assessed by analyzing the resulting reduction in mean squared error. The synthetic data's impact on reducing errors in the wall-bound region is further substantiated by evaluating the mean squared error of the enhanced models.

We have found and examined self-dual solitons within a specific "baby Skyrme" model in two-dimensional space, which is a simplified version of a more complex Born-Infeld theory. The solitons adhere to a framework consisting of a Lagrange multiplier, a constraint, a magnetic field condition, and a boundary requirement. By applying the given constraint and field equation, we've confirmed that the solitons adhere to a self-dual relationship, thus achieving minimal energy. Furthermore, our study involved exploring the properties of numerical solitons under various scalar fields and scalar field ranges.

For a three-dimensional Weyl semimetal model with a constant mass under the influence of an orthogonal magnetic field, our analytical calculations show the emergence of a novel Weyl semimetal phase that breaks time-reversal symmetry within the Hofstadter regime, characterized by zero-hall voltage resistance platforms. Utilizing the Landau band structure derived from the Hamiltonian, we investigate the topological properties and zero-energy surface Fermi arcs of this phase. Notably, our findings reveal the presence of both nodal Weyl points and the Writhing the Worldlines points (Wespuite's the Worldlines points) in this phase's bulk structure.

A novel hybrid nanoantenna has been designed for enhancing the emission capabilities of quantum dots. This innovative approach combines two innovative structures - a hybrid ring and an inverted Y-shaped metal nanotriangle - for optimal performance. A detailed analysis has been conducted of the hybrid nanoantenna system for various material combinations and geometries under different environmental refractive indices. Employing plasmonic materials and carefully optimizing key dimensions, the quantum drive-in effect has been maximized. Specifically, using gold as the metal material yielded exceptional results. Notably, the hybrid nanoantenna system exhibited exceptional brightness and drive-in capabilities in water. Furthermore, by adjusting the positioning of the hybrid nanoantenna relative to the quantum dot, the overall system exhibited remarkable unidirectional directional properties. A thorough examination of the directional emission patterns and system brightness was also carried out for multiple material combinations. A comprehensive analysis of the hybrid nanoantenna system has also been provided through numerical field simulations.

An unusual phenomenon in a granular material's force network has been identified through research. To better understand this phenomenon, scientists developed a model to analyze how the material responds to changes in its boundaries, which turned out to be significantly less sensitive due to a screening effect caused by the material's own structure. The experimental results matched up with numerical models suggesting this phenomenon could occur within the stable state of the material. The findings highlight a significant difference between dry granular materials and their viscoelastic counterparts, opening up a new area of study to explore how screening effects influence the stable state of materials at a basic level.

Utilizing first-principles calculations, our research has examined the structural and electronic properties of silicene in a monolayer configuration on hexagonal boron nitride in the absence and in the presence of manganese decoration. Our findings indicate that undecorated silicene in hexagonal boron nitride in a semimetallic state transforms into a ferromagnetic ferrimagnet when decorated with manganese, exhibiting a remarkable 84.5% reduction in band structure. Undecorated silicene in hexagonal boron nitride is spin-degenerate but becomes ferromagnetic ferrimagnetic when decorated with manganese. The calculated exchange interaction constants for undecorated and manganese decorated silicene suggest the possibility of stable ferrimagnetic ordering. Moreover, undecorated semimetallic silicene becomes a metallic ferromagnetic ferrimagnet when decorated with manganese.

The Sgr A East supernova remnant, situated at the heart of the Galaxy's bulge, is near the supermassive black hole, Sgr A*. Its age, estimated to be around 4-5 million years, has led to varying theories, specifically a Type II supernova or an accretion-driven supernova. Our research, based on the Sh2-109 nebula's spectroscopic data, reveals that the remnant's large size and low-velocity expansion are a result of an interaction between the shock wave from the supernova and the surrounding interstellar gas. The expansion speeds of the shock waves in the remnant's outer regions are notably low, with values of 5.7-7.4 km/s, further supporting the idea of an interaction. By combining our findings with existing models, we have identified the most plausible scenario, which involves the explosion of a Type II supernova in a low-density environment, close to Sgr A*. We have further narrowed down the possible site of the supernova's explosion to a small area, with a radius of 0.1-0.2 parsecs, east of the Sgr A* radio source.

In machine learning, the issue of imbalanced datasets can lead to issues where data with underrepresented classes is under-sampled or causes models to overlook minority classes by oversampling. To address this challenge, various techniques have been developed to improve the accuracy of classifiers. We investigated a range of existing oversampling methods for the classification of multi-class text, including k-nearest neighbor, naive Bayes, and logistic regression. Our study aimed to compare the outcomes of these methods and discovered that the over-sampling algorithm itself does not have a substantial impact, but the choice of feature weighting for each instance is crucial to the overall performance of the classifier.

This study investigates the connections between local news coverage and the COVID-19 pandemic in the 100 largest U.S. markets using a comprehensive dataset of over 145,000 articles from more than 8,000 sources spanning nearly two years. Using an advanced topic model, we categorize nearly 60 distinct themes in COVID-19 coverage and categorize them into four primary groups: the virus itself, public health measures, COVID-19's economic and social impacts, and miscellaneous topics. Through extensive quantitative analysis, we uncover a strong correlation between COVID-19 deaths and market-level measures such as audience size, number of COVID-19 articles published, and specific coverage themes. Notably, our findings reveal that markets with larger numbers of COVID-19-related deaths also tend to have larger populations, a higher percentage of residents without a college degree, and a lower percentage of Black residents. Additionally, our analysis shows that a substantial portion of AI-generated COVID-19 articles incorrectly cites U.S. cases or deaths, while also containing fewer factual sources and citations compared to those generated by humans.

The conservation of angular momentum is crucial in simulating long-term phenomena, especially in astrophysics. Traditional FMAM methods can lead to significant errors in preserving angular momentum, causing problems like orbital decay, which can compromise overall simulation integrity. A new approach, called Conservation-FMAM, is developed to enhance angular momentum conservation within the FMAM framework. This improved algorithm maintains high computational efficiency and can improve preservation of angular momentum by up to an order of magnitude. Conservation-FMAM has been integrated into the FMAM part of the Gadget code and is being tested on basic numerical examples before applying it to a complex simulation of a binary black hole merger. Our results indicate substantial gains in preserving angular momentum, particularly when using large N. These advancements are expected to facilitate more accurate simulations of intricate astrophysical processes.

Numerical studies have been conducted on the $Q^2$ dependence of double spin polarization transfers in relativistic proton-proton elastic scattering. These findings can guide polarization measurements and improve global data analysis using polarization observables. Surprisingly, our results show a significantly higher polarization transfer coefficient ($D_{tt}$) than predicted by phenomenological models at high momentum transfers ($Q^2$), suggesting that accounting for relativistic effects and using proper Dirac and Salam-Ternov polarization evolution is crucial for accurate high-energy proton scattering models.

We explore the problem of efficiently training on a vast dataset by utilizing an expert that takes parameters as inputs. Our primary concern is minimizing memory usage without compromising model performance. To address this challenge, we introduce the amortized data augmentation (ADA) framework, which facilitates efficient learning from experts by processing dataset samples in batches. A key aspect of ADA involves designing a highly expressive data augmentation operator, often an adjustable function that modifies input data. Through our research, we demonstrate the ADA framework can reach statistical optimality, has superior time and memory efficiency compared to other approaches, and is more robust than similar techniques. Furthermore, we show that the ADA framework can significantly scale up the training of expert models, especially in the area of inverse reinforcement learning.

A comprehensive search for the production of two Higgs bosons accompanied by a W or Z boson and leptons or photons in the final analysis is carried out using 2015-2016 LHC data with 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity. The focus of the study is the YHH production mode, where one Higgs boson decays to a WZ pair and the other to a WZ pair, with the associated W or Z boson and leptons or photons in the final state. The analysis is based on the final states consisting of leptons or photons and additional jets. The observed limits on the standard model Higgs boson production modes in association with a vector boson are established, and found to be consistent with the predicted cross sections. The total production cross section for the effective Higgs boson production modes in association with a vector boson is also determined and found to be in agreement with the standard model predictions. The total production cross section for the ZH production mode in association with a Z boson is also estimated and found to be in agreement with the standard model predictions. The production modes of the ZH production mode in association with a Z boson and a lepton or jet in the final state, are also constrained by the study. The results of the study provide further support for the predicted properties of the standard model Higgs boson.

Atomic magnetometers, which measure the Earth's magnetic field and analyze magnetic substances, have seen significant recent advancements. A novel digital magnetometer has been developed using a resonant circuit to detect ferromagnetic materials and measure their magnetization. In an experiment, the performance of this digital magnetometer was tested by detecting the altered magnetization in a nickel sphere following radio-frequency induced magnetic ordering.

For K3 surfaces with an automorphism having a Siegel disk, the associated Picard number falls between $0$ and $18$ and must be an even integer. Conversely, applying the period map, K3 surfaces possessing line or quadric equation automorphisms also display Siegel disks and can be represented by both algebraic and non-algebraic forms.

A supersymmetric model where the lightest neutralino decays into a lightest neutralino and a light scalar has been explored as a viable dark matter theory. Theoretical constraints on this model's parameters are grounded in both dark matter density and neutralino production from light scalars in thermal equilibrium during the early universe. The LHC's null result for neutralino production also provides restrictions on these parameters, particularly when neutralinos have masses less than about 500 GeV. The distinct characteristics of supersymmetry in this particular model result in non-trivial relationships among the gamma ray spectra produced by neutralino pairs. The most prominent feature in such spectra is the presence of a characteristic bump corresponding to the sum of two scalar masses, allowing the ultimate detection of this model if the scalar masses are less than approximately 90 GeV and the neutralino decay occurs within a 10^12 second timeframe. The neutralino's lifetime can be further constrained to less than about 10^12 seconds in some instances. Furthermore, such models may also be restricted by the accumulation of excess energy in the early universe.

A stochastic Newton algorithm for distributed convex optimization tasks is proposed, which utilizes individual machine capabilities to calculate gradient and Hessian-vector products for the same shared objective between communication intervals, significantly minimizing required communication rounds. Convergence analysis for both primal and dual objectives demonstrates the algorithm's efficiency. Empirical evaluations for image restoration and regression demonstrate the algorithm's capability to reduce communication rounds compared to existing methods.

Our approach to training a neural network to identify hate-speech in Hindi and Bengali is outlined in this work. We investigate the viability of leveraging transfer learning for these languages and compare the performance of pre-trained models specifically designed for Hindi and Bengali. An accompanying code repository is released to facilitate future research. Our findings are limited by the languages' low resource status. Our experiment involved a preliminary testing on a tiny dataset of 150 samples for each language to initially assess the feasibility of the method and gather essential insights for subsequent research in the field.

In experiments involving dark matter research and nuclear physics, real-time at-line analysis plays a vital role in identifying key reaction outcomes. Real-time gas-based detectors, utilizing hydrogen as a constituent, can be highly efficient in identifying such reactions due to their versatile ionization capabilities. This review focuses on the concept of using real-time projection chambers as standalone detectors to track reactions occurring within hydrogen. It also highlights advancements in real-time classification algorithms, focusing on machine learning and neural networks, with emphasis on their integration with at-line analytics to identify specific reactions. Additionally, this review explores the potential of real-time projection chambers as more than just detection tools, but as powerful analytical instruments.

Assessing commercial driving based on sensor data can significantly impact truck drivers' livelihoods, but current sensor-based systems have limitations. They often lack a nuanced understanding of driving contexts, can't distinguish between operator errors and mechanical or environmental issues, and make it difficult for fleet managers to pinpoint specific behaviors. Although intelligent and causal methods have been explored, they haven't been widely applied to assess commercial driving safely and effectively. We introduce the CONVERGE system, a collaborative tool that enables informed assessments of commercial driving. It combines expert feedback with sensor data to identify specific driving patterns, minimize false positives, and facilitate more consistent, fair, and informative decision-making processes among fleet managers. A study with real-world fleet managers demonstrated that the CONVERGE system leads to more accurate and consistent results, higher inter-rater reliability, and more nuanced, actionable feedback for individual drivers.

This paper presents a detailed examination of the participants' performance in the 2021 OUT OF VOCABULARY challenge. The competition focused on developing systems that could categorize sentences containing unfamiliar words and missing data. A total of 285 training examples, 299 development texts, and 299 test texts formed the basis of the competition. A comprehensive review of the results indicates that human performance serves as a reliable baseline. Ultimately, eleven distinct approaches were submitted, with the most successful one being a method that combined multiple techniques, including word segmentation, embedding techniques, and a specific type of neural network called the bidirectional long short-term memory model. In comparison, baseline approaches based on domain expertise and general knowledge produced lower accuracy rates. Furthermore, the paper provides insights into areas requiring improvement and potential directions for future research.

Random fields in mathematical models of various complex systems are often defined on intricate, nonlinear surfaces. To analyze their properties, we investigate the geodesic paths within these spaces, particularly those with nonlinear transformations from Gaussian random fields. Utilizing an advanced perturbation technique combined with a series expansion method, we develop a systematic framework to express the geodesic paths in terms of the underlying field's values and their derivatives up to a certain order. We specifically focus on the case of the sine-Gaussian model, commonly known as the Chern-Simons field, to demonstrate that our approach is both efficient and capable of yielding a highly accurate representation. Our findings are validated through numerical comparisons with traditional methods, showing that our approach achieves comparable precision with significantly less computational complexity.
In our research, we conduct experiments on Rayleigh-Taylor Instability by introducing a controlled disturbance through magnetic levitation technology.

For a cuspidal Hecke eigenform $F$ attached to a modular group, compare the $p$-adic L-functions at even integral points to the algebraic normalised Hecke L-function. Boundedness in terms of the prime number $p$ is demonstrated and improved previous results by Chen and Wan. This boundedness has significant implications for the denominators of the special values of L-functions for modular forms.

In a narrow, flat sheet of graphene, researchers have discovered spin-dependent transport phenomena through careful analysis using quantum mechanics. By applying sophisticated simulations, a spin-based Fermi resonance effect in voltage has been identified at specific voltages between zero and six volts. Moreover, in certain configurations, the occurrence of negative resistance was observed. The phenomenon of spin-dependent behavior can be controlled by adjusting key characteristics of the structure, such as its width. The obtained results offer significant opportunities for developing future spin-based devices.

This paper presents proofs of Korovkin theorem analogues in the realm of weakly nonlinear, monotone operators applied to multi-variable Banach lattices of functions. Our study encompasses the almost everywhere convergence, convergence in measure, and $L^{p}$-norm convergence. The discussion is supplemented by several examples that demonstrate the theoretical findings.

A graph on n vertices is called pancyclic if it contains a cycle of every possible length from 3 to n. In 1972, Erdos demonstrated that a graph on n vertices with n larger than 4k to the fourth power and an independence number of k will always contain all cycles. After his findings, he proposed the stronger hypothesis that the graph is actually Hamiltonian. Later, Vaughan, the author, and Perarnaud independently provided proof for Vaughan and Perarnaud's versions of his conjecture, which have now been done.

In the study of 2019 directed flow (p$_{\rm Dir}$) of light charged particles in Au+Au and isobar collisions at a 200 GeV energy level, using the TPC/LHC experiment, new data on p+Pb and Pb+Pb systems were obtained in the same environment as Au+Au collisions, offering a setting insensitive to quark-gluon plasma properties. Analysis revealed that in the very forward rapidity range (0 < y < 5) of the 2019 collisions, a notable difference was found in directed flow between Pb+Pb and Pb+Pb collisions, breaking mirror symmetry and suggesting a variation in the medium's properties near a critical point. A unique signature of directed flow mirror symmetry was observed in the heavy-ion collisions, yet this symmetry was broken in the light-ion collisions due to differing properties of the quark-gluon plasma.

The adaptive spectral Koopman method was designed to solve complex dynamical systems using a data-driven approach. By combining a non-conformal grid-based solution with an efficient adaptive algorithm, the approach provides accurate results while minimizing computational costs. In this work, the method is extended to handle high-dimensional systems by incorporating a sparse-grid based solution, which improves the computational efficiency and enables the analysis of systems with a larger number of variables. A new strategy for constructing basis functions is also proposed, which leverages additional information in the spectral coefficients to improve the performance of the method. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the modified approach, showing comparable performance to the lower-dimensional case while successfully addressing higher dimensional systems.

This review provides a comprehensive overview of theoretical methodologies and findings for an array of atomic, molecular, and solid-state systems subjected to a constant electric field. As the exterior complex scaling method is the primary approach, its fundamentals and the associated numerical techniques are outlined. The focus is on a wide range of phenomena, including ionization in one-electron systems and many-electron atoms, field-induced shifts in energy levels and binding energies, static electron density changes, and the resulting responses of atoms in polar and nonpolar molecules as well as electron-rich materials to an applied electric field.

The Sinkhorn algorithm is widely employed to resolve stochastic Schrödinger problems arising in optimal transport theory. Unconditional convergence of the algorithm is demonstrated when a coupling solution exists, but a example is constructed showing convergence when solutions exist the problem has none, implying convergence of the iterates towards the transport map closure.

The ATLAS experiment at the LHC has recorded data of 294 pb$^{-1}$ in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV in 2017. Using jet and leptonic channels, the cross-section of top-pair production is measured and found to agree with Standard Model predictions, with values ranging from 690 to 720 pb and 680 to 710 pb, respectively.

Key factors that cause a change from a coherent to an incoherent state in ensembles of coupled oscillators have been identified in this study. The incoherent state is characterized by random oscillations, whereas the coherent state is marked by synchronized oscillations. The study focuses on ensembles of oscillators with identical frequencies and is divided into two sub-ensembles. One sub-ensemble remains isolated and the other is divided into smaller groups that interact with the isolated sub-ensemble through central coupling. Each group in the dynamic sub-ensemble contains one or more oscillators, resulting in sub-ensembles labeled S1-S6 and S1C and S2C. As the size of the dynamic ensemble grows, S1, S2, and S3 transform into S1C, S2C, and DC2C, respectively. In contrast, S4, S5, and DC5 remain unchanged. By analyzing the influence of in-phase and anti-phase coupling on coherency, it was found that in-phase coupling tends to maintain coherency, while anti-phase coupling tends to diminish it. The study also reveals varying responses to parameter control, indicating that some systems can be controlled in an orderly manner while others can be controlled chaotically.

We provide sufficient conditions that ensure a function belongs to a specific class, leading to a novel result that generalizes a previous finding by Garg, Singh, and Kumari. Our result yields a sufficient condition under which a function belongs to a class $H_{j+1}$, given $b \leq 0$ and $j$ is a non-negative integer. This condition can be expressed as $Bessel_G^{(j)}_{p+1}(z) \in h_{j+1}([0, \frac{1-|b|}{1+|b|}), 1]$. Our result generalizes a previous finding by Garg, Singh, and Kumari, which can be obtained by setting $b=0$ in our condition.

Dramatic shifts in human behavior due to pandemic-related and underlying pandemic-related trends significantly altered urban life. We created an advanced deep learning system to measure the variety of people encountered in cities, using mobile phone data from 100,000 individuals across ten major European and Middle Eastern cities over two years. We found that pandemic-related factors, such as social inequality and economic interdependence, consistently led to decreased human diversity among friends and family contacts, whereas pandemic-related behavioral changes resulted in significant declines in urban income diversity, which may have far-reaching social implications.

This research focuses on the development of computationally efficient methods for simulating two-phase flow in porous media. As computational power becomes increasingly accessible on parallel architectures, an increasing need arises for algorithms that can utilize any level of available processing units. This study investigates the development of nonlinear field-split (NFS) preconditioners as a solution to this challenge. Specifically, a novel type of NFS preconditioner is introduced, incorporating an explicit representation of the relative permeability and relative viscosity within a decomposition framework. By utilizing an additional degree of freedom within the NFS framework, the performance of these preconditioners can be enhanced, leading to a range of implementations that are explored within the context of two-phase Darcy flow. Two variations of NFS preconditioners are considered: one that employs traditional Schur complement preconditioning and another that leverages an enhanced treatment of the additional degree of freedom. This study demonstrates that incorporating the additional degree of freedom yields a significant improvement in performance, particularly for problems with high nonlinearity. Furthermore, an increase in the order of the flux decomposition results in only marginal improvements, suggesting that a additional degree of freedom within the NFS framework is a more valuable asset than a additional order of the flux decomposition.

A key characteristic of conventional light is its ability to carry chirality through the relationship between color and circular polarization, which is used by certain compounds to absorb specific wavelengths of light in a chiral detection process called CD. This traditional form of light is unique in two aspects - it can selectively interact with left- or right-handed compounds depending on their properties, and it can also be itself, defined as right- or left-circularly polarized light. CD can only be detected using circularly polarized light, which in turn is used by researchers to investigate chiral compounds. This process is widely used, but it's difficult to control and detect circularly polarized light. This problem is overcome by using advanced technology to create ultra-stable laser sources with defined polarization. This allows for the development of more accurate and controlled CD techniques. This study proposes a new laser source based on a cavity that automatically switches polarization direction based on the injected light's chirality. This advanced laser source could be used in various applications, including precise spectroscopy and quantum information processing.

This paper examines how the S-matrix in the Liouville theory is altered when a JT gravity limit is applied, and then connects this to the pseudoparticle type-1 large-$N$ limit of the Pfaffian model. We observe that the deformed JT black hole within this context corresponds to a hot-pink J${\bf CP}^2$ state in the Liouville model, and we calculate how the backreaction caused by the Page mode shifts the puncture position. Additionally, we calculate the J${\bf CP}^2$ area's change due to the page mode's impact. We also outline further investigations into the hot-pink J${\bf CP}^2$ state, the J${\bf CP}^2$ area's change, and the area distribution of the hot-pink J${\bf CP}^2$ state using the Pfaffian model.

A spacetime distortion, or warp bubble, is achieved utilizing negative energy density to enable faster-than-light travel for objects. This concept is embodied in the warp drive solution, which the authors expand upon by adding a positive cosmological constant. This modification is motivated by potential connections between warp drive and dark energy theories in modern cosmology. The researchers find that the adjustment of the cosmological constant's magnitude and sign can yield the same warp drive solutions as introducing negative energy density. Moreover, they extend the original perfect fluid models to include both a perfect fluid and a positive cosmological constant. This is followed by an analysis of the different properties of these generalized warp drive solutions.

As urban populations and their intricate urban frameworks expand, cities increasingly rely on digital twin technology to simulate, visualize, and plan their complex systems. Digital twins, rooted in a unified 3D geographical coordinate system, integrate 3D city frameworks with 2D geographical reference systems, allowing seamless connections between 3D urban frameworks and 2D geographical coordinate systems such as streets, sidewalks, and boundaries. Although digital twin technology has been extensively researched, urban infrastructure data lacks standardized, unified geospatial coordinates, hindering digital twin applications. To address this challenge, this paper introduces GUIDES - Geospatial Urban Infrastructure Data Engineering Solutions, an open-source platform designed to standardize and integrate diverse urban infrastructure data from disparate geographical coordinate systems into a unified, hierarchical framework. GUIDES' architecture is illustrated, along with its experimental results and validation through well-known urban infrastructure datasets from public sources, demonstrating its efficacy in facilitating digital twin technology.

We introduce a technique, spin dephasing, which enables the precise measurement of the temperature and equilibrium distribution of motion in the ground state of a single ion. The technique's resolution is on the order of 0.1 millikelvin, allowing for the detection of minute changes in temperature. By analyzing noise patterns introduced by coupled ions, state distributions can be reconstructed with high accuracy. Additionally, this method can be used to detect cooling rates of optical bibles at rates as low as 10 to the power of 9 per second. The experiment's findings show a deviation from the predicted Pegg-Kumar distribution by the Coulomb crystal, indicating a level of ground state purity of 95.8 percent plus or minus 0.1 percent. Furthermore, this technique's analysis of heating patterns in the Coulomb crystal reveals a power-law relationship with a power index of 8, strongly suggesting interaction with the p-photon Leakyy potential. The technique's simplicity and low measurement impact could make it a valuable tool for investigating quantum systems with low ground state purities.

TERS technology combines tip-enhanced Raman scattering and scanning near-field optical microscopy capabilities and is crucial for chemical imaging at the nanoscale, yet the mechanisms behind its operation are still unclear. We present a new framework that integrates various factors, including electromagnetic, chemical, and electromagnetic-induced charge transfer effects, for the first time using ab-initio near-field theory. This theory models the near field enhancement factor as a sum of distinct terms. Our approach is demonstrated for the enhancement of Raman signals in benzene and in Au/InAs nanostructures, showing significant agreement with existing experimental data and highlighting the importance of the electromagnetic effect under certain conditions. Notably, our results reveal substantial non-local chemical and electromagnetic enhancements that could facilitate detection of raman-inactive vibrational modes and contribute to understanding TERS's exceptional sensitivity.

We have made initial SKA-like radio observations to the centers of nearby galaxies, including the Local Group members, to detect potential anomalous microwave emission. This type of emission is thought to originate from small particles within the interstellar medium, commonly observed in the Milky Way but its presence in nearby galaxies remains uncertain due to limited past studies. Using the Sardinia Radio Telescope, we conducted multi-band observations at eight bands, which included three bands at K-band frequencies, on 11 galaxies at distances of up to 800 kpc. The observations revealed radio bright emissions in eight galaxies, although clear distinct peaks were not observed. This study serves as a pilot investigation to examine the feasibility of detecting AME in nearby galaxies, which will be further explored by next-generation low-frequency SKA-like telescopes.

A notable entropy change is observed in ferrielectric ammonium sulfate near its transition temperature, however, the underlying cause of this phenomenon remains unclear. We demonstrate that this large entropy change is primarily due to the substantial rotational entropy of the ammonium ions. Moreover, the observed effect is intrinsically tied to the ferroelectric phase transition. We have also identified similar entropy changes in two additional ferroelectric compounds, (CH3NH3)2PbI3 and tetramethylammonium malonate, which exhibit entropy-temperature relationships that are parabolic in nature.

In reinforcement learning (RL), agents make decisions by predicting outcomes, updating their understanding of rewards as their predictions differ from actual results. However, studies have shown that people don't always act in a way that maximizes their rewards. A large cross-sectional study of 21,142 participants, including those without a RL background, revealed variations in RL strategies correlated with brain activity, specifically in response to unexpected rewards. A 2-step model RL strategy was found to be associated with elevated activity in the brain when experiencing rewarding surprises, whereas a 1-step model showed such activity in response to unexpected rewards in the future. These variations were found to be relatively consistent across time in a smaller longitudinal study of 20 participants. These results suggest an innate tendency in humans to RL strategies that do not yield the best results may be evolutionarily advantageous.

A proposed Witting configuration, with a different complexity of 360 elements, may help clarify relationships between quantum entanglement and contextuality in quantum theory. This novel setup, based on the reduction of a complexified $E_8$ root system, will be used to explore physical phenomena related to quantum mechanics in a single spacetime dimension. The different $W_7^{red}$ systems are found in different contexts in string theory's various dimensions. The differences in their real vector space dimensions highlight an interesting property. The configuration will help to clarify relationships between quantum phenomena in simple systems in 1+1 dimensional spacetime by replacing a previous understanding of it in a more complex setting.

The continuous Fréchet distance c-approximate near neighbor problem involves pre-processing a set of curves to efficiently find nearby query curves within a certain factor. Specifically, we aim to develop an algorithm that can efficiently identify curves that are significantly close to the query curves, under the continuous Fréchet distance metric. Our solution proposes a data structure that efficiently identifies curves that are significantly close to the query curves, using a specific amount of additional memory and allowing for a specific query query efficiency. We start with a known algorithm for a simplified version of the problem involving disjoint segment queries and extend it to handle queries consisting of multiple moving points, resulting in curves with distinct vertices.

A key factor in quantum computing is the need to develop techniques that can correct for errors caused by imperfect quantum circuit measurements. Although previous methods existed to correct for these errors, some faced significant computational burdens, rendering them only feasible for small-scale problems. In response, a novel method called iterated measurement error mitigation (IM-EIM) has been developed to correct for these errors. This new approach combines with a technique called iterative Bayesian unfolding to correctly estimate original probability distributions from distorted measurements. Experimental results from various quantum devices have demonstrated the effectiveness of this method in accurately recovering probability distributions. Furthermore, the iterated IM-EIM method surpasses its baseline method in a real-world application of physics.

In the realm of human-robot interaction, particularly when operating robots such as automated driving, conventional hand signals serve as an integral means of conveying intent. However, developing protocols that enable robots to comprehend human intentions poses a significant challenge. A novel paradigm known as Shared Autonomy, where control is shared between human and robot through a shared interface, offers promising potential. By utilizing this shared interface, we can design an information-exchange protocol, demonstrating its effectiveness through experiments involving both humans and robots operating under Shared Autonomy. Our results show that under Shared Autonomy, a more accurate model of human intentions can be developed compared to traditional human-robot interaction, thereby increasing the frequency of appropriate robot responses.

For mobile robots to navigate unfamiliar surroundings independently, they need an accurate map representation. Existing representations have their drawbacks; for example, a topological map is lightweight but inflexible for navigation, while a geometric one is adaptable for navigation but heavy and impractical for a swarm of robots to create efficiently. This research presents a novel, hybrid representation of a mesh-coordinated tree-based map to address these challenges, incorporating the advantages of both geometric and topological maps. We propose an updated version of the A* pathfinding algorithm for navigating through detailed meshed maps and demonstrate our proposed representation outperformed others in terms of path efficiency and consistency when navigating various layouts.

Research into two-dimensional arrays with near perfect correlation properties has gained significant interest. Two primary sets of such arrays, known as Z-complementary array code sets and inter-group complementary code sets, have been studied extensively. Several novel designs of these code sets have been proposed using multivariable functions, including a new construction method using Nielsie's equation. However, this construction method can result in a relatively small set size. In this paper, we successfully generate inter-group complementary code sets and two-dimensional Z-complementary array code sets with larger set sizes. These code sets are created using multivariable functions, specifically generalized permutational equation sets and an equation involving the Legendre symbol.

Computed tomography (CT) is a widely used medical imaging technique for diagnosing internal injuries and conditions, but the images it produces can be compromised by noise and degradation. To counteract these issues, an advanced model has been developed that combines various image enhancement techniques in a single framework. This model uses mathematical methods to remove noise from images, including those captured from multiple energy wavelengths, and to separate the different materials in a sample into distinct groups. By doing so, it can yield clearer, more detailed images and a more accurate representation of the materials being studied. Extensive testing has shown the model's image enhancement and material decomposition capabilities on various CT datasets with different noise levels. CT datasets can be obtained from the open-source XCAT phantom library, and this code is available for others to study and enhance the model.

We investigate how electron spillover and nonlocal behavior affect light propagation between two metallic structures separated by extremely small dielectric spaces to understand their influence on light-matter interactions. Using quantum theories, we compare real electron distributions and nonlocal responses to simplified models to identify the conditions under which they yield significant results. Our findings indicate that a particular spillover model accurately represents the true electron behavior, while the standard spillover model fails to capture the correct physics in certain situations. Furthermore, we discover that a system's nonlocal response becomes significant when the metal-dielectric interface exhibits a dielectric constant greater than about 10. Our conclusions are validated by examining experimental results for previously studied nanoparticle dimers.

In this research, we investigate the user's part in Contextual Named Entity Retrieval (CNER), where users seek to extract specific entity mentions based on given context. Our focus is on improving all-lexical retrieval methods, which efficiently handle multiple entity types but struggle with disambiguation using basic documents. To address this limitation, we have developed an entity-specific phrase mining approach that draws inspiration from term relevance feedback in information retrieval systems. By utilizing a modified method that retains results' quality while enhancing the efficiency of the feedback process, we generate more accurate phrase features that clarify which entities are involved. Through our comprehensive evaluation on four datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, which outperforms the baseline by 3-11% in terms of average precision at top 60.

Time-based data, such as multivariate time series and longitudinal data, are ubiquitous in decision-making processes across various fields. Despite the recent advancements in data visualization, effective exploration of complex data types remains a challenge. This limitation is further compounded by the absence of interactive features. Our research aims to address this gap by developing a graphical display that supports interactivity, allowing users to efficiently navigate and compare multiple time series. Our innovative approach, featuring unique visual mechanisms like the "time ribbon" and "time bar," enables interactive displays of time-based data, including filtering, zooming, and the simulation of hypothetical scenarios. The effectiveness of our solution is demonstrated through a study involving 15 participants, who utilized our dashboard to analyze COVID-19 data in real-time, showcasing its potential to facilitate informed decision-making.

The vast repository of electronic health records (EHRs) presents a challenge in mining useful information due to their heterogeneous and unstructured nature, rendering conventional methods ineffective. A recent technique, the SimGNN model, addresses this challenge by exploiting the implicit graph structure of EHRs to perform semi-supervised learning. However, the SimGNN model overlooks the heterogeneous nature of EHR nodes and aims to learn node embeddings solely for classification, which may not be conducive to EHR data similarity. In response to these limitations, a novel approach called HetEGBNN is proposed, which integrates the heterogeneous information of EHR nodes and edges, using the attention mechanism to represent each node and edge adaptively, thereby enhancing the learning process. Furthermore, HetEGBNN incorporates the principles of the continuous-time Kramers equation to achieve dynamic node embedding continuity. Our comprehensive evaluations using three publicly available EHR datasets highlight the superior performance of HetEGBNN in comparison to seven baseline models.

This study explores the impact of solvent influence on the behavior of electric double layers surrounding charged soft surfaces immersed in electrolyte solutions, using molecular dynamics simulations. An asymmetric electrolyte solution is modeled to study the effects of solvent model variations, including explicit solvent models with differing numbers of solvent particles and water based solvent models. Simulation results show that solvent polarization affects the structure of electric double layers and potential distributions around the surfaces, with the solvent acting as a dielectric medium influencing surface properties. Analysis of the density profiles and average solvent orientations within the electric double layers reveals that solvent polarization affects ion behavior and potential distributions, thus altering surface properties. Ultimately, solvent polarization has a significant effect on the behavior of electric double layers and the properties of the surfaces they surround.

Automating the labor-intensive and error-prone process of extracting requirements from unstructured text is a highly challenging task. To address this challenge, we propose a novel deep learning-based approach that leverages limited annotated data to produce high-quality extraction results. By integrating the power of deep learning models, our solution effectively uses domain-specific knowledge to enhance the accuracy of extracted unstructured data. To demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed approach, we conducted a user study on a real-world dataset, comparing the performance of our method with state-of-the-art techniques and showing a significant improvement in extraction quality.

This research focuses on developing an energy-efficient strategy within a network-coded system, which minimizes total power consumption for data transmission from source to destinations in two-phase, with optimal power distribution between source and relay nodes, and scheduling for relay nodes. Utilizing a new energy metric in the first phase, we implement a relay scheduling technique that results in symmetric transmission, and a joint power-scheduling strategy is applied for the second phase to reduce power consumption. Our proposed strategy outperforms previous works, which failed to consider joint scheduling and power allocation in both phases, and demonstrated an 80% reduction in power consumption.

A theoretical framework that uses the Dirac equation to model a specific type of magnetic state, known as a Yu--Shiba--Rusinov state, has been developed through first principles. The model's accuracy was tested by comparing its predictions with experimental and other theoretical results for a specific scenario, involving a single manganese atom on a niobium surface and pairs of manganese atoms on the same surface.
