We also evaluate four existing data augmentation techniques to compare their relative effectiveness. Our experiments show that these new methods outperform the existing techniques and significantly enhance the robustness of the models against adversarial examples. The implementation of our research is publicly available.

Researchers aim to create meta-learning algorithms that capitalize on previous experiences to efficiently learn new tasks by representing them in a consistent framework. We've developed MetaLE, a novel meta-learning algorithm designed to produce a linear representation for any task within a specific class, maintaining this consistency across tasks. Unlike existing methods, MetaLE doesn't require the task class to be predefined in advance. Our results demonstrate that, with sufficient data from a limited number of linear representation tasks, MetaLE can determine an optimal representation for each new task while ensuring it adheres to past experiences, with a computationally efficient time complexity.

Achieving high performance multilingual machine translation using deep learning often requires substantial resources, including large models trained on extensive datasets from major language groups. To overcome this limitation, researchers have explored methods like model distillation and quantization, which allow for knowledge transfer from large, well-performing models to smaller, less resource-intensive versions. These approaches, however, have limitations, including a loss of performance when the smaller models are applied to new language pairs, and the resulting models often lack the ability to generalize effectively. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel hybrid method that combines distillation and quantization, producing a compact translation model that matches the performance of its larger, high-performance counterpart and can be easily applied to new language pairs. Experimental results confirm that this approach surpasses the other methods, especially when compared to simple fine-tuning of a smaller model, and offers a promising path towards multilingual language technology adoption in resource-constrained environments.

The edge graph of an alternating cycle hypergraph, assuming every edge has an even number of vertices, creates a complete graph with a balanced coloring. We've found a single 10-vertex hypergraph whose edge graph is also completely connected, demonstrating that the edge graph can indeed represent a complex hypergraph structure. From the existence of such a hypergraph, it follows that there is an irrational Lagrangian density for a hypergraph with 7 vertices and 3 edges.

The accuracy of chest X-ray diagnosis is significantly improved by finding abnormal areas related to respiratory conditions, specifically pneumonia. To address challenges associated with limited medical expertise and extensive labelled data requirements, this research focuses on reducing the amount of labelled data needed for pneumonia detection. We examine the effectiveness of various data enhancement techniques in improving pneumonia detection accuracy. By employing the Mean Integrated Squared Error (MISE) metric, we assess the performance of different image enhancement techniques, including Color Jitter, and analyze their impact more closely. Furthermore, we examine the effectiveness of combining color jitter with other image enhancement techniques, such as random erasing, as well as the impact of using our proposed method on the AUC, F1-score and DICE scores in the dataset.

Existing image captioning models often fail to produce diverse captions due to limited options for users to control the content generated. This limitation makes it difficult to generate customized captions that meet specific user requirements. In this research, we introduce the concept of prompt learning for image captioning, which enables users to control the generated captions by inputting different prompts. This study aims to develop efficient learning methods for complex neural captioning models that can generalize across various prompts. Two such methods are presented: Learn-to-Generate (LTG) and Prompt Learning with Weight Sharing (PLWS), which allow for flexible and scalable learning processes. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms existing image captioning models, and also reveals the importance of designing effective token interactions in controlling generated captions.

As autonomous systems become increasingly prevalent, it is essential to establish legal and ethical frameworks for addressing harm caused by these systems to individuals. The current approach in the field of autonomous systems has primarily focused on the concept of foreseeability, which is too limited to establish foreseeability as a fundamental criterion for establishing the causation of harm in autonomous system design. A more effective method involves examining the definition of harm from moral and legal perspectives, and analyzing how digital representation contributes to the identification of harm. A mathematical framework has been proposed to evaluate harm, demonstrating the connection between digital representation and the evaluation of causation through moral and legal definitions. This framework provides a basis for analyzing foreseeability within this context.

This study showcases MMLSpark, an innovative open-source library that bridges the gap between Cognitive Toolkit and Apache Spark by introducing Java bindings and new components. The integration with OpenCV and the development of automated PySpark wrapper generation tool expands the functionality and usability of the platform. The utilization of AutoML in Spark-generated wrapper code and a case study on the utilization of existing Spark machine learning and distributed computing capabilities for deep learning model training with Pytorch highlight the potential for improved efficiency and scalability in large-scale data processing. The demonstration of these concepts was executed across multiple Amazon EC2 clusters located in various availability zones.

Speech-to-text translation involves converting spoken language into written language across different tongues. Conventional two-stage approaches using speech recognition and machine translation have inherent flaws, including the amplification of inaccuracies. By contrast, single-system methods offer improved performance but are complex to implement. We introduce a novel zero-shot speech-to-text translation method that requires neither target language speakers nor model training for the target language. Instead, it leverages data from the model's source language to make it functional for the target language. When used in conjunction with an existing translation model, it achieves comparable results to the top single-system methods, as evidenced by automatic and manual evaluations.

This study introduces a novel extension of the traditional heat equation, incorporating the flux's time derivative under dynamic boundary conditions. A quasilinear parabolic equation of the form $u_t - \Delta p(u) = f$ with $Q(p(u)) = 0$ is considered, where $Q$ represents the Gurtin operator. Here, $u$ is the temperature, $p(u)$ is the thermal stress, $f$ is the internal heat source, $Q(u)$ is the boundary flux, and $Q'(0) = 0$ at a critical point. The boundary conditions become second-order differential equations in this scenario. Assuming $Q$ exhibits strict convexity, we establish that the solution maintains $C^{2,1}$ regularity up to the boundary using a barrier function approach. Furthermore, if $Q$ has a second derivative at zero, we introduce dynamic boundary conditions for $Q'(0) > 0$ that yield piecewise continuous, bounded $u_t$ inside the domain and $Q(u)$ on the boundary. These conditions also lead to a positive absorbing set. Finally, if $Q$ has a negative second derivative at zero, we introduce dynamic boundary conditions for $Q'$(0) < 0 that allow for the existence of unique, bounded pieces of the solution. These conditions also facilitate the global attraction of the absorbing set by the weakly stable equilibrium solution.

Precise short-term electricity consumption forecasts are crucial for managing low voltage networks efficiently, particularly with regard to sustainable energy management. Our approach combines probabilistic energy consumption predictions from multiple models with calibrated uncertainty, leveraging the Weibull distribution to facilitate the fusion of these forecasts. This is combined with an optimization-based method focused on forecasting daily peak times rather than overall profile shapes, yielding more accurate and reliable forecasts. Our study demonstrates that the integration of these techniques outperforms established forecasting methods, such as those based on historical forecast data or the Kalman filter.

The growth of machine learning algorithms has not kept pace with the increasing demand for expert knowledge to avoid the time-consuming process of labeling large datasets. We aim to provide a comprehensive overview of various forms of expert knowledge and the machine learning methods that can integrate them, with a focus on the key characteristics of each knowledge type, the essential requirements for effective integration, the major approaches for incorporating expert knowledge, the open challenges in this field, and the future directions for research. By addressing these issues, we hope to promote further study in the area of global machine learning tools and frameworks.

The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has posed a significant threat to public health, with hospital overflows and staff shortages limiting the ability to test and treat patients efficiently. In such circumstances, non-invasive diagnostic methods like chest X-rays and CT scans become vital tools for diagnosing patients remotely and reducing the risk of infection to medical staff. To address the shortage of healthcare workers, deep learning-based methods have been developed to detect COVID-19 and other respiratory diseases such as tuberculosis and pneumonia from CT scans. However, the lack of annotated lesion-level data in current COVID-19 detection datasets hinders the development of advanced segmentation and localization algorithms. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the first unbiased COVID-19 dataset, which is specifically designed to localize and segment COVID-19 affected areas in CT scans, unlike existing datasets that are biased towards the center of the image. This dataset is annotated using a weakly supervised learning approach, which allows for the development of more realistic and effective lesion localization and segmentation algorithms. Furthermore, we introduce a series of innovative network architectures to learn lesion representations and perform boundary regression and segmentation tasks, including a two-stage framework combining weakly-supervised detection and segmentation models, and a single-stage detection-segmentation task-based model. Our results show that these models achieve promising outcomes in comparison to existing datasets, and we further examine the impact of different data modalities and annotation modalities on the performance of our proposed frameworks.

This paper presents a detailed description of the method we used in the
August 2020 challenge of the International Society for Computed Tomography in
Orthopedics, where we were vying for best performance in automatic vertebrae
localization and identification using CT. Our approach involved two key
components: a deep learning-based method to pre-process the data and a
model that used anatomical knowledge to solve the problem. The method that
pre-processed the data used a deep learning model to transform the images in a
way that made the vertebrae stand out, and then a second deep learning model
was used to help find the vertebrae. The method that used anatomical knowledge
was a method that used a different approach of breaking the problem into
smaller parts and solving each part separately, and then using that to help
find the vertebrae. In the end, the method performed very well, setting new
records for a challenge that had been going on for years.

Our theory explores the behavior of electron collisions with a strong repulsive barrier in a confined space under intense interaction with a light source. As the strength of the light source increases, the energy levels of the system become entangled, resulting in the system's energy states to be determined by the combined influence of the light source and electron spin. In this region, the electrons' behavior is significantly altered, and the system's energy levels exhibit complex patterns of interference. Furthermore, the influence of the light source not only modifies the system's energy states but also stabilizes the system's dynamics by inducing oscillations in the electrons' movement. These findings are supported by theoretical calculations and offer new insights into the interaction between light and matter at extremely strong intensities.

The employment of elastic actuators in quadruped robots has been proven effective
for enhancing dynamic walking capabilities and improving actuator efficiency.
This efficiency is attributed to the synergy between the actuator's elasticity
and dynamic control, along with the elasticity's contribution to jumping and
locomotion. Nevertheless, current approaches to achieving this synergy are
divided into two separate stages, with the first stage focusing on designing
actively compliant actuators and the second stage on developing a controller
that considers their characteristics. This two-step process, however, prevents
the complete exploitation of the actuator's elasticity. This article proposes
a unified approach, combining actuator design and control within a single joint
learning framework, thereby enabling quadruped robots to take full advantage
of their elastic actuators.

We propose a novel variational scheme for estimating the separability norm, a critical factor in quantum key distribution security assessment, and apply it to detect entanglement in two-qubit and three-qubit systems. The method is implemented using the Hermite-Gaussian basis and allows for increased flexibility in the three-qubit scenario. We conducted multiple benchmark tests, comparing the variational method with established entanglement detection techniques, including the positive partial transpose, to evaluate its performance. We also performed a first-order stability analysis to confirm the method's convergence.

A well-documented phenomenon called a small-scale electron temperature gradient driven instability occurs when electrons try to adapt their non-Maxwellian distribution with a free energy gradient to match their thermal state. Past research focused solely on fluid models, which often failed to capture essential features found in collisionless environments. A new, more complex kinetic simulation reveals significant differences, including distinct magnetic flux and spatial structures that are more complex and narrower than fluid models predict. The results suggest that electron distribution non-thermal effects significantly impact the gradient's flow and displacement. Furthermore, this effect could influence other plasma phenomena such as the tearing mode and kinetic Alfvén waves, particularly when they have finite magnetic forces.

A surge in interest has accompanied the resurgence of historical fashion trends.  Due to the limited availability of detailed fashion images, AI is now being utilized to extract features from images and identify similar ones through fashion retrieval.  Researchers have previously attempted to perform fashion item-level retrieval, but this approach fails to capture the nuanced differences between fashion items and their distinct characteristics, such as the color of a shirt.  To rectify this, we propose a Feature-Level Attribute Manipulation (FA2) technique for semi-supervised fashion image retrieval.  FA2 employs a feature-level generator to create more general features and an attribute discriminator to ensure the discriminator's features are not overly specific.  By doing so, it enables the classifier to learn a broader fashion representation and the subsequent retrieval of similar images based on their distinct attributes.  Notably, unlike previous methods, FA2 enables the retrieval of query images without the need for additional training, but rather relies on the feature generator and attribute discriminator for improved performance.

The $\R$-optimal solution for the underdetermined equation $Ax=y$ where $A$ is a bounded linear operator mapping a Banach space to a Hilbert space, along with specific parameters, is represented by a curve that can be reformulated as an operator-dependent flow based on the Helmholtz decomposition of the space. This curve is proven under particular conditions to constitute a one-parameter group, with its generator being the dual of the part of the A operator that operates within the space's range's orthogonal complement,op, provided the range of the A operator,op, constitutes a subspace within the space's range,op. This reformulation of the curve is achieved by reformulating the corresponding operator, A*, as a dual, or conjugate, gradient operator for solving equations that are challenging to solve due to their underdetermined nature. This reformulation is made possible by reformulating the corresponding operator, A*, as a dual, or conjugate, gradient operator for solving equations that are challenging to solve due to their underdetermined nature. This reformulation is significant as it sheds new light on the theoretical justifications of the Tikhonov regularisation method. This curve is extended in this work to solve linear inverse problems in the form $Ay=y^0+\xi$ in the case where noise is present, under the assumption of certain conditions. This reformulation of the curve is achieved in the case where noise is present in the form of an invert

Constructing the matching cost is a critical step in estimating light field depth but existing methods fall into two limitations: either the cost is bin-based and disregards actual pixel values or it relies on pixel-based values and doesn't account for occlusions in the light field data. In this paper, a novel cost constructor called block-based warping and flow depth map restoration (BWFR) cost constructor is proposed. The proposed method combines the advantages of bin-based and pixel-based approaches by warping nearby light field images using an estimated optical flow to derive depth maps. Due to pixel warping effects, the proposed method can utilize values from multiple images at the same location, making the depth estimation more accurate. Moreover, occlusions in the light field data are addressed by warping the source images using estimated optical flow before warping them to the target image. The proposed method's unique depth map restoration process allows warping sources from various directions to the target location. Experiments show improved depth estimation accuracy of up to 11.7% compared to the state-of-the-art method.

This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, first reducing the system and then employing double Wronskian solutions to yield a range of novel solutions for the equations, including solutions tied to the discrete spectrum, bound states, and resonant phenomena. Additionally, this work is further extended to a higher-order FL equation system, resulting in newly derived solutions for this higher-order system, with solutions being characterized as asymptotically different from those found in the Schrödinger equation context.

Our analysis reveals that actions within double field theory inherently embody a non-Riemannian nature. By developing a method to generalize the Hodge-de Rham complex in double field theory, we demonstrate that this approach is equivalent to theoretical frameworks employing non-Riemannian geometry, specifically stringy Finsler-Dirac and 4-vector spaces. We discover that the double field theory framework can be seen as a stringy model for Finsler spaces with odd dimensions, and we show that the theories based on stringy Finsler spaces and 4-vector spaces are continuous, smooth extensions of both 10-dimensional superstring theories and M-theory. Additionally, our theoretical frameworks exhibit a smooth, continuous path connecting them with Einstein-Hilbert and Gauss-Bonnet theories.

In dense home WiFi networks, most users don't actively switch between Access Points due to lack of awareness of available options and their benefits. Most home WiFi networks have several Access Points from the same manufacturer, and their wireless extender devices automatically connect to the nearest AP, but lack awareness of optimal network conditions.  Our proposed smart wireless extender solution uses IEEE 802.11k/v protocols to monitor and switch clients between APs, improving performance and efficiently utilizing network resources. Our simulation results show that our proposal significantly improves network throughput and reduces delays compared to traditional methods, and offers better results than a competitive solution that switches clients between APs, but doesn't account for network conditions.
